newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond mart sighs with relief after CPI.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond mart sighs with relief after CPI.

text.p: Corporate bond players breathed a sigh of relief on Tuesday following a benign report on U.S. inflation at the retail level, dealers said.
Despite the good news very light activity was seen in secondary trading with spreads remaining unchanged, they said.
Earlier, the Labor Department reported a 0.1 percent rise in March consumer prices, while CPI, excluding food and energy, increased by 0.2 percent.
The tame inflation report triggered a rise in U.S. Treasuries sending the 30-year T-bond up over a point to end the trading day up 29/32 at 94-7/32 to yield 7.09 percent.
"It's been pretty quiet in the corporate secondary market with probably better sellers than buyers," said one high-grade trader. "The new issue calendar seemed to be driving the market today."
In the primary sector various issuers took advantage of the improved rate environment to issue debt, players said.
A&P sold $300 million in 144A 10-year notes to yield 100 basis points over Treasuries, dealers said.
Also, Service Corp International set $250 million in 7.375 percent seven-year notes to yield 58 basis points and $200 million in 7.70 pct 12-yr notes to yield 83 basis points.
Also tapping the market was NationsBank's wholly owned trust, NB Capital Trust IV, with $500 million in 30-year capital securities to yield 118 basis points.
Dealers said more debt issuance is on the horizon.

Meanwhile, concerns that a strong CPI figure could extend the recent weakness in the stock market had high-yield players cheering as they watched the Dow Jones Industrial Average climb through the day, posting a 135 point gain at the close.
A stock sell-off was expected to further unsettle investors and trigger a flight to quality, high-yield experts said.
In the high-yield sector, prices ended 1/4 to 1/2 higher on the positive news, traders said.
"Things are defintely firmer," said one junk trader. "Although it hasn't been that active the market, overall, is stronger," he added.
In the supermarket sector prices were mixed with Grand Union paper quoted off 1/2 at 95-1/4 bid, 95-3/4 offer, while Ralph Grocery's 10.45 percent debt traded up at 103-3/4 bid, 104-1/4 offer.
Pathmark 12 percent debt was also a bit weaker at 94 bid, traders said.
